sources.entry: DragonFly - A small MTA for home and office use. Works on Linux and FreeBSD. BSD-3-Clause C

summary.one_liner: dma (DragonFly Mail Agent) is a small mail transfer agent for home and office use that accepts mail from local mail clients and delivers it locally or to remote servers.
summary.what_it_does: dma accepts outgoing mail from locally installed Mail User Agents and delivers it either to local mailboxes or to a remote destination. Remote delivery supports TLS/SSL and SMTP authentication. The README says it is not a replacement for large MTAs like sendmail or postfix, and it does not listen on port 25 for incoming connections. It is built with make on Linux, and with a separate bsd directory for BSD systems. Installation is done with make install plus link and directory targets, and the README points to an INSTALL file for requirements and configuration options.
use_cases: send outgoing system mail from a home server
relay local mail through an external SMTP provider
lightweight mail delivery for a small office
replace a heavy MTA on a single-user machine
send cron or script notification emails
how_to_run: Install: make install sendmail-link mailq-link install-spool-dirs install-etc
notable: Small, purpose-built MTA for home and office rather than a full mail server
Does not accept incoming connections on port 25
Supports TLS/SSL and SMTP authentication for remote delivery
Available through FreeBSD pkg, Ubuntu apt, and Arch packages
caveats: Not intended as a replacement for full MTAs such as sendmail or postfix
Does not listen for incoming mail on port 25
Configuration requires reading the separate INSTALL file
